welch.name: Welch PSD
welch.definition: SciPy Welch PSD: average of segment periodograms; parameters come from the module configuration and installed SciPy defaults.
welch.limitations: Different call sites use different segment lengths. Preserve configuration and SciPy version; no claim that all call sites share one estimator configuration.

references.citation: Welch PD (1967). The use of the fast Fourier transform for the estimation of power spectra.

aperiodic.name: Log-log robust aperiodic screening
aperiodic.definition: Theil-Sen fit of log10 PSD against log10 frequency after configured exclusions; exponent=-slope, intercept and median absolute residual retained.
aperiodic.limitations: Not specparam/FOOOF; excluded bands and positive-power masking define the PRAYCG screen.

references.citation: Sen PK (1968). Estimates of the regression coefficient based on Kendall's tau.

erp.name: Recipe-defined ERP and Morlet power
erp.definition: Trial baseline subtraction, trial mean and SEM; Gaussian complex carrier sigma=cycles/(2*pi*f), truncated to min(half epoch, ceil(3.5*sigma*fs)), L2 normalization, convolution power averaged across trials; baseline ratio in dB.
erp.limitations: PRAYCG operational implementation, not a validated named ERP component. No zero-mean wavelet correction or cone-of-influence exclusion; epoch boundaries can bias power.

connectivity.name: Band-pooled spectral connectivity
connectivity.definition: Hann-window FFT; cross spectra averaged over frequencies within each epoch and then epochs. Coherence=abs(mean cross)^2/(mean power x * mean power y); PLI=abs(mean sign(imag cross_epoch)); wPLI=abs(mean imag cross_epoch)/mean abs(imag cross_epoch).
connectivity.limitations: wPLI is not debiased squared wPLI. Band pooling differs from frequency-resolved estimators. Signed imaginary coherency is mirrored into both matrix triangles; it must not be interpreted as a conventional antisymmetric imaginary-coherency matrix. References identify lineage, not estimator equivalence.

references.citation: Vinck M et al. (2011). An improved index of phase-synchronization for electrophysiological data in the presence of volume-conduction, noise and sample-size bias.
Nolte G, Bai O, Wheaton L, Mari Z, Vorbach S, Hallett M (2004). Identifying true brain interaction from EEG data using the imaginary part of coherency.
Stam CJ, Nolte G, Daffertshofer A (2007). Phase lag index: assessment of functional connectivity from multi channel EEG and MEG with diminished bias from common sources.

pac.name: Binned phase-amplitude modulation index
pac.definition: Mean amplitude per phase bin, normalize to probabilities p; MI=(log(K)+sum(p*log(p)))/log(K), empty bins initially zero.
pac.limitations: Tort-style modulation index; filtering, surrogate construction and trial handling are PRAYCG-specific. MI alone does not establish physiological coupling.

references.citation: Tort ABL, Komorowski R, Eichenbaum H, Kopell N (2010). Measuring phase-amplitude coupling between neuronal oscillations of different frequencies.

bh.name: Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment
bh.definition: Sort p-values, multiply by comparison count/rank, apply reverse cumulative minimum and restore order.
bh.limitations: The code supplies the family of comparisons. Appropriate dependence assumptions and family definition remain necessary.

references.citation: Benjamini Y, Hochberg Y (1995). Controlling the false discovery rate: a practical and powerful approach to multiple testing.

sample_entropy.name: Sample entropy and coarse-scale screening
sample_entropy.definition: Aligned m and m+1 embeddings; unordered non-self pairs within Chebyshev distance r*SD; SampEn=-log(A/B). Missing when either pair count is zero.
sample_entropy.limitations: Coarse-graining uses non-overlapping means, but tolerance is recomputed at each scale rather than fixed to original-signal SD. Complexity input may be stride-decimated without a new antialias filter. Do not present this as equivalent to canonical multiscale entropy.

references.citation: Richman JS, Moorman JR (2000). Physiological time-series analysis using approximate entropy and sample entropy.
Costa M, Goldberger AL, Peng CK (2002). Multiscale entropy analysis of complex physiologic time series.

permutation_entropy.name: Normalized permutation entropy
permutation_entropy.definition: Delayed ordinal patterns with stable sorting for ties; Shannon entropy divided by log(order factorial).
permutation_entropy.limitations: Ties are assigned by temporal index, not discarded or jittered; result depends on recipe order and delay.

references.citation: Bandt C, Pompe B (2002). Permutation entropy: a natural complexity measure for time series.

lz.name: Binary parsing complexity screen
lz.definition: Binary parsing count c normalized by c*log2(n)/n.
lz.limitations: Lempel-Ziv lineage only. Equivalence of this parser to a reference implementation has not been certified; do not claim independent authorship from its header.

references.citation: Lempel A, Ziv J (1976). On the complexity of finite sequences.

spectral_entropy.name: Normalized spectral entropy
spectral_entropy.definition: Welch PSD over 1 Hz to min(45 Hz, Nyquist); normalized positive-bin probabilities; entropy/log(number of bins).
spectral_entropy.limitations: A PRAYCG operational bandwidth-limited entropy measure, dependent on sampling and frequency resolution.

references.citation: Welch PD (1967). The use of the fast Fourier transform for the estimation of power spectra.

microstates.name: Run-local polarity-invariant topographic clustering
microstates.definition: GFP-peak centered maps; unit-norm topographies; absolute-correlation assignment and principal-eigenvector centers; seeded restarts with GFP-squared weighted explained variance.
microstates.limitations: Update centers are unweighted within each cluster although restart selection is GFP-weighted. No canonical A-D labels, cross-run alignment or temporal smoothing; states sorted by coverage.

references.citation: Pascual-Marqui RD, Michel CM, Lehmann D (1995). Segmentation of brain electrical activity into microstates: model estimation and validation.

csp.name: Train-fold CSP and ridge discriminant decoding
csp.definition: Trace-normalized uncentered trial.T@trial matrices averaged within class, generalized eigenproblem C0 v=lambda(C0+C1)v, extreme eigenvectors; log normalized projected variance.
csp.limitations: Uncentered covariance differs when means are nonzero. CSP fitted in training folds; trial-level cross-validation does not establish subject/session generalization.

references.citation: Ramoser H, Mueller-Gerking J, Pfurtscheller G (2000). Optimal spatial filtering of single trial EEG during imagined hand movement.

lda.name: PRAYCG ridge linear discriminant
lda.definition: Pooled within-class covariance with trace-scaled ridge, pseudoinverse and equal-prior linear discriminant scores.
lda.limitations: Custom implementation, not a claim that scikit-learn LDA ran. Frozen regularization and split design matter.

rsa.name: Sensor-time split-half representational distances
rsa.definition: Flatten sensor-time features; even/odd condition mean differences; mean product weighted by inverse diagonal-shrunk residual variance. Optional Spearman upper-triangle model comparison with condition-label permutations.
rsa.limitations: Noise precision is estimated using all trials, not independent training data. Do not label this fully unbiased crossnobis. Negative distances are retained; sensor-level representations are not localized brain mechanisms.

references.citation: Kriegeskorte N, Mur M, Bandettini P (2008). Representational similarity analysis: connecting the branches of systems neuroscience.
